title: Lenis smooth-scroll experiment

environment.browser: Headless Chrome via Chrome DevTools Protocol
environment.profile: Fresh Chrome profile for each probe; browser cache cleared before warm-up
environment.sourceCommit: acbdd68 plus uncommitted Phase 2/3 work and Phase 4 changes

validation.buildWarning: Existing chunk-size warning only; no new build errors or warnings from Lenis.

integration.animationLoop: Lenis autoRaf; existing section rAF loops left untouched
integration.nativeSmoothConflict: html.lenis { scroll-behavior: auto; } disables the existing scroll-smooth behavior while Lenis is mounted
integration.touch: syncTouch: false; native touch scrolling preserved
integration.anchors: Custom capture-phase same-page anchor handler using useLenis, pushState, and popstate; Lenis anchors option disabled
integration.nestedScroll: data-lenis-prevent on the mobile navigation panel and the full-menu dialog

deepLink.note: The #story deep link already failed before Phase 4. The #menu deep link worked in both builds. This is a pre-existing issue, not introduced by Lenis.

observations: Wheel input became visibly smoother: four trusted 120px wheel events produced 40-44 distinct scroll positions with Lenis versus 5 with native smooth scrolling.
All tested navigation targets and history entries matched the native baseline; differences were the same fixed-header offsets as before.
Sticky positioning, resize correction, and the hero final frame matched the baseline.

Lenis programmatic glides are longer than native smooth scrolling, especially short jumps: CTA last movement was about 1.6s with Lenis versus about 0.85s native; the short Experience anchor was about 1.14s versus about 0.50s.

Story direct-scrub lag varied between Lenis runs (max 1-8 frames); the 8-frame runs are within the Phase 3 production range of 8 frames. One run showed three duplicate decode sources, which did not reproduce.

Fast wheel scrubbing through the Story skipped some intermediate frames, as expected when one wheel event moves several frames; the visible target stayed within 4 frames and settled on the target frame.
The #story deep link already failed in the native baseline; #menu deep links worked in both builds. This is pre-existing and outside Phase 4.
limitations: Headless desktop Chrome only; no real-device or physical touch testing, so no real-device improvement is claimed.
Mobile smoke used emulated mobile metrics with a desktop user agent, not a real phone.
No throttled-network or low-end-CPU profile was run.
Reduced-motion wheel input and the reduced-motion Story/Hero mapping were not separately re-measured; the programmatic navigation path was measured, and the scroll-linked mapping code is unchanged.
The direct-scrub probe calls window.scrollTo while Lenis is active; that test-only path can interact with Lenis native-scroll synchronization and is not the normal wheel path.
Programmatic glide duration was not tuned to match native smooth scrolling exactly.
